concept-map:
Create a polished technical documentation infographic for Lakehouse Plumber. Match this established visual system: warm off-white #FAF8F5 canvas, charcoal #202126 text, thin vermilion #E65337 arrows, pale apricot #FCEBDE cards with apricot #F4A261 accents, subtle rounded corners. Bold Cabinet Grotesk-style titles and clear Satoshi-style body type. Flat editorial layout, no 3D, no ornamental pipelines, no gradients, no logo, no watermark. High resolution. Prefer a nearly square or modest landscape canvas so text is legible in a documentation article. Use the exact labels requested. Every arrow must have a clear meaning and direction. Generous spacing, concise text, no crossings through text or cards.
Title: "How LHP fits together".
Top small banner: "YAML is the authoring format".
Main composition: a large central/right container labelled "Pipeline" with subtitle "Deployment grouping". Inside it, TWO distinct containers side by side labelled "Flowgroup: orders" and "Flowgroup: customers". Inside EACH flowgroup, three compact action tiles connected left to right: "Load" → "Transform" → "Write". Add a small detached tile "Test" inside EACH flowgroup, with NO data-flow arrow to Write. A shared line below these two groups inside Pipeline says "Actions connect through named views". The two flowgroups are examples; do not imply a fixed count.
LEFT of the pipeline container, three small separate helper cards stacked vertically: "Blueprint + instance" with subtitle "Expands flowgroup patterns"; "Template + parameters" with subtitle "Adds actions"; "Preset" with subtitle "Applies settings".
Connect Blueprint + instance with a thin arrow to the outer border of a flowgroup, label "expands". Connect Template + parameters with a thin arrow to the action area of a flowgroup, label "adds actions". Connect Preset with a thin arrow to the action area, label "applies settings". These helper cards are OUTSIDE the pipeline, not parent objects or runtime stages. Avoid crossing these three connectors.
Below everything: a simple left-to-right strip "Environment values" → "LHP generation" → "Lakeflow Python". The Pipeline has one downward arrow to LHP generation. Footnote exact: "Files are not deployment units: one YAML file can describe multiple flowgroups."
Only this content. Do not claim templates create pipelines, presets create actions, or one blueprint always creates one pipeline.

Title: "Reuse settings, actions and flowgroups".
Design THREE clearly separated horizontal rows, each a concrete example, labelled 01 PRESET, 02 TEMPLATE, 03 BLUEPRINT.
Row 01: a card "bronze_defaults" with "maxFilesPerTrigger: 200", an arrow labelled "shared reader setting" to two small target labels "orders" and "customers". An additional smaller card "high_throughput" with "maxFilesPerTrigger: 1000" points ONLY to orders. Final outcomes explicitly labelled "orders: 1000" and "customers: 200". Do not show 200 as orders' final setting. This row demonstrates matching actions inherit settings with flowgroup preset applied after template preset.
Row 02: a card "bronze_ingest" containing a tiny "Load → Write" pattern. Two branches labelled "entity: orders" and "entity: customers" lead to separate cards "orders_ingest" with subtitle "CSV → orders" and "customers_ingest" with subtitle "JSON → customers". Group both result cards in a container labelled "Pipeline: bronze". Make clear same action pattern, different parameters.
Row 03: a card "tenant_bronze" with subtitle "orders + customers patterns". Two branches labelled "tenant: acme" and "tenant: globex" lead to containers "acme_bronze" and "globex_bronze", EACH holding small pills "orders" and "customers". Small annotation: "2 patterns × 2 instances = 4 flowgroups". This is a separate blueprint example from row02; DO NOT connect row02 to row03 as one runtime flow.
Footer exact: "Presets change settings. Templates add actions. Blueprints expand flowgroups."
No additional text, no guessed YAML values or extra entities.

Create a polished technical documentation infographic for Lakehouse Plumber. Bold Cabinet Grotesk-style titles and clear Satoshi-style body type. Flat editorial layout, no 3D, no ornamental pipelines, no gradients, no logo, no watermark. High resolution. Title: "One definition. Different environments."
Two visually distinct horizontal bands labelled "BUILD TIME" and "RUNTIME".
Build-time band:
A compact top sequence of three boxes: "Local variables" with token "%{name}" → "Template + preset expansion" with token "{{ parameter }}" → "Environment substitution" with token "${catalog}".
Below this sequence, a card "Same flowgroup YAML" with monospace line "${catalog}.bronze.orders" fans into two branches. Branch left: "substitutions/dev.yaml" → "dev_catalog.bronze.orders". Branch right: "substitutions/prod.yaml" → "prod_catalog.bronze.orders". Label the two final cards "Generated Python". No real credentials.
At the bottom of the build band a separate small secret-reference card: "${secret:sales_db/password}" → "Generate a lookup call" with monospace "dbutils.secrets.get(...)". A clear line separates the build and runtime bands.
Runtime band:
An arrow crosses down from the lookup-call card to a box "Databricks executes the lookup". A separate "Secret scope" box points INTO this execution box, labelled "Secret value". Small footer exact: "The reference is resolved during generation; the value is fetched at runtime."
Do not imply secrets are written into generated files or that the secret lookup happens before deployment. Logical scope names can resolve differently per environment. Keep complex token text large and spelled exactly.

Title: "Same changes. Different table history."
A top shared timeline labelled "One key: 42 · sequence order" with three events, left to right: "1 · Basic" → "2 · Plus" → "3 · Pro". These are three updates for the same key; use no dates or deletes.
Below, three equal vertical panels:
Panel 1 title "Append", subtitle "Keep each incoming row", simple table with column headers "key | tier | sequence" and exactly three rows "42 | Basic | 1", "42 | Plus | 2", "42 | Pro | 3". Footer "No per-key update".
Panel 2 title "CDC · SCD1", subtitle "Keep current state", simple table headers "key | tier" with exactly one row "42 | Pro". Footer "Latest value per key".
Panel 3 title "CDC · SCD2", subtitle "Keep version history", a timeline with "Basic [1, 2)", "Plus [2, 3)", "Pro [3, open)" in sequential segments. Footer "Track changes to tier".
Below these three panels, a separate wide band titled "When the source provides snapshots". Show "Snapshot 1: Basic" → "Snapshot 2: Plus" → "Snapshot 3: Pro" → "Compare snapshots" → "Choose SCD1 or SCD2". It must be visually clear snapshots are a different INPUT format, not a fourth history type. Do not draw a snapshot arrow to Append.
Bottom caption exact: "LHP generates the flow definition. Lakeflow applies the changes."
Use very clear grid alignment; do not add unrequested values or claim exactly-once behavior.

Create a polished technical documentation infographic for Lakehouse Plumber. Match this established visual system: warm off-white #FAF8F5 canvas, charcoal #202126 text, thin vermilion #E65337 arrows, pale apricot #FCEBDE cards with apricot #F4A261 accents, subtle rounded corners. Title: "Monitor pipelines from one place".
Top slim strip labelled "GENERATED BY LHP": "event_log + monitoring" → "Notebook + view pipeline + job".
Below, a large runtime area with TWO consecutive numbered task containers.
Container 1 heading "1. Collect event logs". Inside its left side, three small stacked source cards labelled "Bronze event log", "Silver event log", "Gold event log". Each source feeds a separate small stream line with an individual label "Own checkpoint". The three lines converge into one larger card "Shared Delta event table". A label above the three lines says "Independent available-now streams". These lines are data flow; no bronze-to-silver-to-gold arrows.
A right-pointing arrow leads from task1 to container2, labelled "Then".
Container 2 heading "2. Refresh summary views". It reads the Shared Delta event table and produces a card "events_summary" with concise sublabels "Run status", "Duration", "Row metrics". This is a materialized view. Keep the output card inside task2. Make the data read clear without crossing the task-order arrow.
Below task2, a small dashed optional card "Optional job correlation", with a small source label "Databricks SDK". No automatic alerting or dashboard imagery.
Footer exact: "The monitoring job collects logs before refreshing views."
Second small footer: "Summary views are configurable; job correlation is opt-in."
Show default monitoring shape. No hidden dependencies on LHP at pipeline runtime, no direct business-data reads, no automatic source discovery while the notebook runs. Minimal clear orthogonal arrows.
